reason: Attention includes bottom-up, stimulus-driven processes; it is broader than top-down control, not a kind of it.
Spreading activation is a specific search mechanism within semantic networks; the relation is inverted/mechanism-of, not is-a.
Working-memory demand is unrelated to attributing mental states to others.
Positive feedback is one form of reward; the relation is inverted (parent is narrower than child).
Drawing inferences is a distinct process that may support choosing, not a kind of selecting among alternatives.
Spatial attention is defined by spatial coordinates in any modality; it cross-cuts rather than specialises visual attention.
Salience is a stimulus parameter that drives attention, a cause/property rather than a kind of attentional process.
Reading is decoding symbols for meaning (also possible by touch); visual recognition is at most a component of it.
Interference is the disruptive effect that control must resolve, not a kind of top-down control.
Lexical selection is a stage (part) of word production, not a kind of it; no definitions available.
Response conflict is one cause of difficulty, not a kind of perceived effort.
The orienting response is a reaction triggered by detecting novel or salient stimuli, a consequence rather than a kind of detection.
Movement is the change of position being supervised; motor control is the function governing it, not its superclass.
Pain is a sensory and emotional experience usually caused by nociception, not a kind of noxious-stimulus encoding.
Extinction is new learning that reduces a conditioned response; it is context-dependent but not a kind of context memory.
Prosocial behaviour is action toward others, related to but not a kind of processing information about conspecifics.
Risky decision making is a kind of decision making; impulsivity is a trait that may influence it.
Extracting risk information is an input to choice, not itself a selection among alternatives.
Engagement is a component/phase contrasted with shifting and disengagement, not a kind of shifting.
